The Evolution of the MacBook  The MacBook is a brand of Macintosh notebook computers designed and marketed by Apple Inc. that use Apple's macOS operating system since 2006. It replaced the PowerBook and iBook brands during the Mac transition to Intel processors, announced in 2005. Launched for the first time in 2006, the first Macbook was quite massive, but its functions sparked the interest of many people. So Apple continued to launch new models that are more and more efficient and modern. MacBook, MacBook Air and MacBook Pro were laptops for everyone's needs, and for Apple fans, they completed the Apple ecosystem for a much easier use of all Apple devices. Now, the latest Macbook came in 2022 with the new Apple M2 processor and is proof of the longevity and evolution of the entire series of Macbooks from Apple. The MacBook family was initially housed in designs similar to the iBook and PowerBook lines which preceded them, now making use of a unibody aluminum construction first introduced with the MacBook Air. This new construction also has a black plastic keyboard that was first used on the MacBook Air, which itself was inspired by the sunken keyboard of the original polycarbonate MacBooks. The now standardized keyboard brings congruity to the MacBook line, with black keys on a metallic aluminum body. The lids of the MacBook family are held closed by a magnet with no mechanical latch, a design element first introduced with the polycarbonate MacBook. The Memory, drives, and batteries were accessible in the old MacBook lineup, though the newest compact lineup solders or glues all such components in place. All of the current MacBooks feature backlit keyboards. In this video you will see how the Apple MacBook has evolved over time.
